label: John 21:1
text: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.

label: John 21:2
text: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.

label: John 21:3
text:
Simon Peter said to them, “I’m going fishing.”
They told him, “We are also coming with you.” They immediately went out, and entered into the boat. That night, they caught nothing.

label: John 21:4
text: But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach, yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus.

label: John 21:5
text:
Jesus therefore said to them,
“Children, have you anything to eat?”

They answered him, “No.”

label: John 21:6
text:
He said to them,
“Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.”
They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish.

label: John 21:7
text:
That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!”
So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around him (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea.

label: John 21:8
text: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.

label: John 21:9
text: So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid on it, and bread.

label: John 21:10
text:
Jesus said to them,
“Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”

label: John 21:11
text: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fish, one hundred fifty-three; and even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.

label: John 21:12
text:
Jesus said to them,
“Come and eat breakfast.”
None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.

label: John 21:13
text: Then Jesus came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise.

label: John 21:14
text: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples, after he had risen from the dead.

label: John 21:15
text:
So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter,
“Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?”
He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.”
He said to him,
“Feed my lambs.”

label: John 21:16
text:
He said to him again a second time,
“Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?”
He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.”
He said to him,
“Tend my sheep.”

label: John 21:17
text:
He said to him the third time,
“Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?”
Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time,
“Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.”
Jesus said to him,
“Feed my sheep.

label: John 21:18
text: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself, and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you, and carry you where you don’t want to go.”

label: John 21:19
text:
Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him,
“Follow me.”

label: John 21:20
text: Then Peter, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ breast at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray You?”

label: John 21:21
text: Peter seeing him, said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”

label: John 21:22
text:
Jesus said to him,
“If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

label: John 21:23
text:
This saying therefore went out among the brothers, that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but,
“If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”

label: John 21:24
text: This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.

label: John 21:25
text: There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.

label: Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias
statement: After these things Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias (21:1) - a resurrection appearance to the disciples by that lake.
note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly; the naming evidence for 'the sea of Tiberias' is entered on claim:jn-06-01-sea-called-tiberias, which this scene reuses (related_to), not on this appearance claim.

label: Seven disciples were together by the lake: Peter, Thomas, Nathanael of Cana, the sons of Zebedee and two others
statement: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee and two other disciples were together (21:2); only John names this group after the resurrection.

label: The disciples fished from the boat through the night and caught nothing
statement: Peter and the others entered the boat that night and caught nothing (21:3); night fishing was the ordinary working method on the lake (Luke 5:5 'we toiled all night and took nothing').

label: At the stranger's word they cast the net on the right side and could not draw it for the multitude of fish
statement: They cast the net at the stranger's word and were not able to draw it for the multitude of fish (21:6) - a miracle claim.
note: Miracle claim, searched honestly; the evidence entered attests the fishing practice and the lake's fishery, never the catch.

label: The beloved disciple recognized the risen Jesus and Peter threw himself into the sea
statement: The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter 'It is the Lord!'; Peter wrapped his coat around himself and threw himself into the sea (21:7).
note: John's detail alone; the P66/Sinaiticus first-hand variant of this verse assimilates Luke 5:5's wording (see the passage variant).

label: The boat was about two hundred cubits from land
statement: The other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from land but about two hundred cubits away (about 90-105 m on the common cubit), dragging the net full of fish (21:8).

label: A charcoal fire (anthrakia) with fish laid on it and bread on the shore
statement: On the land they saw a fire of coals (anthrakia) with fish laid on it, and bread (21:9) - a shore breakfast cooked over a charcoal fire.
note: The same rare word anthrakia as John 18:18's courtyard fire (related_to); both occurrences are John's.

label: The net held 153 large fish and was not torn
statement: Peter drew the net to land, full of great fish, one hundred and fifty-three; and for so many the net was not torn (21:11) - the exact count is John's detail alone.

label: The risen Jesus served the disciples bread and fish on the shore
statement: Jesus said 'Come and eat breakfast', took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise (21:12-13) - the risen Jesus eating with the disciples.
note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly. Luke 24:42-43 knows a different appearance meal (broiled fish in Jerusalem); the fish-eating motif is shared, the scenes are not the same event.

label: This was the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he had risen
statement: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead (21:14) - John counts the appearances of John 20 plus this scene.
note: Appearance claim; John's own counting (20:19-23 evening, 20:26-29 with Thomas, 21:1 by the lake). The Synoptics count differently; no external evidence.

label: The threefold question 'do you love me' and commission 'feed my sheep' to Peter
statement: Jesus asked Simon Peter three times 'do you love me', Peter answered three times, and Jesus commissioned him 'Feed my lambs... Tend my sheep... Feed my sheep' (21:15-17).
note: John's private rehabilitation scene after the denials (18:17, 18:25-27); no external evidence.

label: Jesus predicted that when Peter is old another will gird him and carry him where he does not wish - signifying the death by which he would glorify God
statement: 'When you were young you girded yourself... when you are old you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish' - 'this he said, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God' (21:18-19).
note: The verse never says 'crucifixion'; the martyrdom reading is tradition. 1 Clement (c. 96) is the earliest witness that Peter died a martyr's death; the Roman crucifixion setting and the upside-down detail are later and disputed (see the claim's documented_by).

label: The saying circulated among the brothers that the beloved disciple would not die, and John corrects it
statement: Peter asked about the beloved disciple; Jesus answered 'If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?'; the saying went out among the brothers that this disciple would not die, and the evangelist corrects it (21:20-23).
note: A report of early Christian rumor corrected in the text itself - John's detail alone, no external evidence.

label: The beloved disciple testifies to these things and wrote them, and 'we know his witness is true'
statement: 'This is the disciple who testifies about these things and wrote these things; we know that his witness is true' (21:24) - the Gospel's own claim that the beloved disciple was its eyewitness author.
note: Modern scholarship is divided: most scholars read 21:24 as claiming the beloved disciple authored the Gospel, others as a later group endorsing his testimony (fetched Gospel of John article); the identification of the beloved disciple with John son of Zebedee rests on reception (Irenaeus, Papias), graded D here.

label: The world itself could not hold the books of everything Jesus did
statement: 'There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself would not have room for the books that would be written' (21:25) - the Gospel's final word on its own selection.
note: The twin of 20:30-31 (related_to); a statement about the book's selection, not an event.
